issues.legal_issue: Part-performance protection cannot establish title or support an affirmative suit for a declaration of ownership or other rights in immovable property.
material_facts: The claimant relied on a written agreement to sell and possession said to have been given under it.
He sued for a declaration that the land was not liable to attachment and sale and sought injunctions against the sale and interference with his possession.
The agreement had not been registered, although local law required its registration.
issues.conclusion: The agreement and the doctrine of part performance could not establish title or support the declaration sought; part-performance protection operates as a shield to retain possession, not as a sword to assert title or obtain affirmative relief.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act creates a statutory bar against a transferor enforcing certain rights against a qualifying transferee in possession, but confers no title or interest and is available as a defence, not as an independent cause of action. A contract for sale does not itself create title or an interest in the property under Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, and registration requirements arise under Section 17 of the Registration Act. The Court relied on Ram Gopal Reddy v. The Additional Custodian Evacuee Property; Delhi Motor Company v. U.A. Basrurkar; Sardar Govindrao Mahadik v. Devi Sahai; Sheth Maneklal Mansukhbhai v. M/s. Homusji Jamshed-ji Ginwalla & Sons; and Technicians Studio Pvt. Ltd. v. Lila Ghosh.

predicates.suit_seeks_affirmative_property_relief: The claimant brought a suit seeking a declaration or other affirmative relief concerning rights in immovable property.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_part_performance: The claimant relied on possession or acts said to have been done under an agreement to transfer the property.
predicates.claimant_seeks_to_establish_title_or_an_: The claimant relied on the agreement and part performance to establish ownership or an independent right, rather than only to resist enforcement against possession.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks affirmative property relief based on part performance to establish title or an independent right, part performance cannot support that relief.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who participates in a fraudulent, sham transaction and does not approach the court with clean hands cannot obtain the protection of part performance.
material_facts: The claimant sought protection based on an agreement made with the judgment debtor's wife after the land had been attached.
The High Court found that the agreement was sham and fraudulent, that no consideration had been paid, and that it was brought into existence to defeat the creditors' rights.
The High Court found that the claimant was privy to the fraud and that his alleged possession was a device to protect the debtor's property.
The claimant sought a declaration and injunctions rather than relying on part performance only as a defence to retain possession.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to protection under Section 53-A, and the Court dismissed the petition challenging the High Court's decision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act protects a transferee in possession only when the statutory conditions are met, including performance or continuing willingness to perform the transferee's obligations; the protection is equitable and requires the claimant to come to court with clean hands. The Court explained that the section imposes a bar on the transferor and does not create title, and relied on the principles in Sardar Govindrao Mahadik v. Devi Sahai and the other authorities addressing the defensive scope of Section 53-A.

predicates.proceeding_seeks_part_performance_protec: The claimant sought to rely on possession under an agreement to transfer property for protection against enforcement concerning that property.
predicates.claimant_is_party_to_sham_or_fraudulent_: The claimant participated in a sham or fraudulent transaction brought about to defeat another person's lawful claim.
predicates.claimant_lacks_clean_hands: The claimant's conduct in obtaining or relying on the transaction was inequitable.

issues.definition: A claimant seeking part-performance protection is denied that protection when the claimant participated in a sham or fraudulent transaction and lacks clean hands.
